name: Lift External Link Notice
author: bradleywatson

sections.description:
Lift External Link Notice adds a configurable leaving-site notice for external links. It is designed for websites that need a clear outbound-link disclosure, including financial institutions, healthcare organizations, associations, and other compliance-sensitive sites.

The plugin does not require Elementor, Elementor Pro, popup builders, custom link classes, React, or build tooling. Once activated, it watches normal frontend links, ignores same-domain links, skips whitelisted domains or URLs, and shows a modal notice before the visitor continues to an external site.

Features:

  • Intercepts normal external link clicks on the frontend.
  • Ignores same-domain, hash, empty, javascript, mailto, tel, admin, and editor links.
  • Optional whitelist for trusted domains or full URLs.
  • Optional whitelist for subdomains beneath the configured site host.
  • Continue and cancel button labels can be edited.
  • Empty button labels hide that button.
  • Overlay, modal, text, title, button, and hover colors.
  • Font family selector.
  • Pixel-based style controls for modal width, spacing, typography, padding, gaps, and border radius.
  • Global responsive controls with optional desktop, tablet, and mobile overrides.
  • Live desktop, tablet, and mobile preview in the WordPress admin.
  • Overlay click and Escape-key closing options.
  • No visitor tracking and no external services.
  • Master enable/disable toggle for turning the notice on or off without deactivating the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Lift External Link Notice in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Lift External Link Notice.
  4. Configure the notice content, whitelist, behavior, and styling.
  5. Test an external link on the frontend while logged in and logged out.
sections.faq:
Does this require Elementor?

No. This is a standalone WordPress plugin and works without Elementor.

Does this use a popup builder?

No. The notice modal is built into the plugin and configured from a normal WordPress settings page.

Will this affect internal links?

No. Same-domain links are ignored. You can also whitelist trusted external domains or full URLs.

Will this always show for external links?

The notice handles normal link clicks and keyboard activation when JavaScript is enabled. Internal links, trusted entries, downloads, and non-web protocols are skipped. Browser actions such as middle-click, context-menu opening, directly entering a URL, and navigation by other scripts are outside this click handler. This plugin does not guarantee legal or regulatory compliance.

Which subdomains are trusted?

With subdomain trust enabled, only descendants of the configured site host are trusted, ignoring its leading www prefix. For example, a site at tenant.example.com trusts child.tenant.example.com, but sibling.example.com needs an explicit whitelist entry. Full URL entries also match the scheme and port.

Does this plugin contact external services or track visitors?

No. The plugin does not send visitor data to external services and does not track visitors.
sections.changelog:
1.0.6

  • Prepared the audited settings, whitelist, accessibility, and editor-preview fixes for release.
  • Updated compatibility metadata following supplied live testing on WordPress 7.1.3.

1.0.5

  • Fixed loss of literal backslashes when saving settings and safely handled malformed settings and invalid colors.
  • Limited automatic subdomain trust to the configured site host and respected ports in full URL whitelist entries.
  • Restricted the JavaScript open API to eligible HTTP(S) external URLs.
  • Kept keyboard focus within the notice, restored background interaction on close, and supplied an accessible name for empty titles.
  • Made whitelist count and validation messages translatable.
  • Preserved reviewer-approved identifiers, include paths, and asset URL handling.

1.0.4

  • Derived the plugin URL from the main plugin file so assets load correctly regardless of the installation directory name.

1.0.3

  • Updated plugin globals, classes, functions, settings, admin actions, and JavaScript objects to use the unique liftexli prefix.
  • Rebuilt the WordPress.org submission package under the lift-external-link-notice slug.

1.0.2

  • Shortened the plugin name shown in WordPress plugin info to Lift External Link Notice.
  • Updated the plugin author display to Lift Group while keeping it linked to the Lift Group site.

1.0.1

  • Added Lift Group branding to the settings page.
  • Added a master enable/disable toggle for frontend notice behavior.

1.0.0

  • Initial standalone release.

upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Sites hosted below a parent domain must add trusted sibling domains explicitly to the whitelist. The JavaScript open() API now follows the same eligibility rules as maybeOpen(); it no longer forces notices for internal or whitelisted URLs.
